question:
(i) Explain why the formation of a rainbow is mainly due to dispersion and not diffraction.
(ii) Compare dispersion and diffraction in terms of the physical cause of each phenomenon.

options.A:
(i) A rainbow is mainly due to refraction, internal reflection, and dispersion in water droplets. Different wavelengths have different refractive indices and deviate by different amounts.
(ii) Dispersion is caused by wavelength-dependent refractive index in a medium. Diffraction is wave spreading around an obstacle or aperture whose size is comparable to wavelength.
options.B:
(i) A rainbow is mainly caused by diffraction through water droplets.
(ii) Dispersion occurs only at narrow apertures, while diffraction is due to refractive index variation.
options.C:
(i) A rainbow forms because all colours have the same deviation in water.
(ii) Dispersion and diffraction are the same phenomenon.
options.D:
(i) A rainbow is formed by polarisation only.
(ii) Diffraction occurs because the speed of light depends on wavelength in a medium.
